item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is substantially closer to the frozen contract: it adds the requested convenience API using the established multipart helper while keeping the change narrowly scoped. A introduces explicitly forbidden association APIs and unrelated retry/body-ownership changes.","reasons":["B uses `multipartbody.NewFile(\"file\", fileName, content)`, producing the required replayable multipart body with the correct field and filename.","B preserves `FilesService.Add` unchanged and naturally propagates reader errors returned by `NewFile`.","A adds `WithFilesFormFields` and `NewFileWithFields`, directly violating the contract not to add association fields and to reuse `multipartbody.NewFile`.","A refactors raw request replay and changes closing semantics for seekable bodies, despite the explicit instruction not to refactor unrelated retry machinery; this creates a broad behavioral change beyond file uploads."],"risks_a":["`Upload` bypasses `FilesService.Add`, duplicating its request, decoding, and error path.","The new seekable-body replay mechanism changes public behavior for every raw request and may introduce ownership or shared-seeker hazards.","The required source-reader-error case is not visibly tested."],"risks_b":["`Upload` also bypasses `FilesService.Add`, so option handling and response behavior remain duplicated instead of centralized as required.","Tests omit explicit validation and source-reader-error coverage.","The retry test confirms two attempts but does not verify that the uploaded multipart content is intact on the retry."]}
